rubric_part: Part G - Model Evaluation and Comparative Analysis

dataset.name: UCI Default of Credit Card Clients (#350)

generalization.regime: Higher bias / Linear boundary (slight underfit vs trees)
Higher bias / Linear boundary (slight underfit vs trees)

critical_discussion.performance_differences: On the 6,000-row held-out split, E2 Ensemble (2:1) leads F1 (0.5458), while E2 Ensemble (2:1) leads ROC-AUC (0.7787). Distinct precision-recall operating profiles emerge: GB achieves Recall=0.6285 / Precision=0.4699; RF achieves Precision=0.5032 / Recall=0.5953; E2 (2:1) blends them to F1=0.5458, Precision=0.4981, Recall=0.6036, ROC-AUC=0.7787; and LR trails at F1=0.5208 / ROC-AUC=0.7593.
critical_discussion.overfitting_underfitting: Train-to-test F1 gaps follow model capacity: LR=+0.0155 (low variance, mild linear underfitting vs nonlinear tree splits), GB=+0.0145 (shallow depth-2 trees keep fit tight), RF=+0.0491 (regularized depth-18 / leaf-16 leaves with 0.0% singletons), and E2=+0.0388 (interpolates between RF and GB). All CV-to-Test F1 shifts remain compact, indicating negligible threshold/selection overfit on the training CV.
critical_discussion.computational_efficiency: Measured identically under single-threaded n_jobs=1 on 24,000 train / 6,000 test rows: LR is fastest (0.13s fit, 9.8ms predict, 2.8 KB), GB is compact (6.75s fit, 15.0ms, 43.7 KB), RF requires 7.65s fit / 188.9ms / 7748.6 KB across 400 depth-18 trees, and E2 combines RF + GB costs (14.38s fit, 198.7ms, 7804.5 KB).
critical_discussion.model_interpretability: Interpretability decreases along LR (white-box standardized log-odds across 91 features) -> GB (150 depth-2 additive stumps) & RF (400 depth-18 trees audited at mean depth 17.88) -> E2 (opaque weighted average (2/3)*p(RF) + (1/3)*p(GB)). On out-of-sample permutation importance, top F1 driver is LR=PAY_0, GB=PAY_0, RF=PAY_0, E2=PAY_0.
